## 任务 1：§4.3 32B 分析移至 Appendix（释放空间）

**当前**：`experiments.tex` L87-89，§4.3 "32B Model-Specific Analysis" 约 8 行正文。

\subsection{32B Scale}\label{sec:32b-analysis}

Results at 32B are exploratory$^\dagger$ ($n{=}19$--$20$; MDE 8.6--9.5pp; \cref{app:power_analysis}). ## 任务 2：扩展 §5 Discussion and Conclusion

**当前**：`discussion.tex` 仅 3 句话。利用 §4.3 释放的空间扩展到 8-10 句。

**新 Discussion 结构**（替换整个 `\section{Discussion and Conclusion}` 内容）：

```latex
\section{Discussion and Conclusion}\label{sec:discussion}

\paragraph{Implications for safety probing.} Our central finding---that metric choice alone produces a 14--61 layer divergence and qualitatively reverses HS advantage conclusions---has direct methodological implications. Safety probing studies should report results under multiple layer selection criteria rather than a single researcher-chosen metric; layer selection should be treated as a key specification choice alongside model architecture and dataset. The cosine compression mechanism (\cref{app:cosine_volatility}) provides a geometric explanation: shallow-layer representations compress directional information, causing crossing-rate metrics to select layers where probes operate near the noise floor.\looseness=-1

\paragraph{Relationship to probing methodology.} Metric sensitivity in probing is well-documented~\citep{belinkov2022probing}; Voita and Titov's MDL probing~\citep{voita2020information} was proposed precisely to reduce metric dependence. Our contribution is demonstrating a \emph{cascade} effect specific to temporal safety probing: metric $\to$ layer $\to$ conclusion, where the severity (14--61 layer gap, sign reversal) far exceeds what prior work documents at a fixed layer. This cascade arises because safety probes operate across generation steps rather than across inputs, creating a temporal dimension where layer selection interacts with representation geometry.\looseness=-1

\paragraph{Boundary conditions.} The HS advantage is confirmed at 7--8B (+20--22pp, nested CV) but conditional: it diminishes from 4/4 to 1/4 significant models with stronger text encoders (384d $\to$ 1024d), suggesting the advantage may partly reflect encoder capacity ceilings rather than intrinsic HS superiority. Position partially mediates the advantage (2/4 quadratic). Whether residualization removes a genuine confound or a correlated signal requires causal interventions on position encoding---a key direction for future work. Our ensemble (\cref{tab:ensemble}) and mitigations (\cref{app:practical_mitigation}) offer lightweight defenses, though false positive rates (11--50\%) preclude deployment.\looseness=-1
```

注意：这段大约 3 个 paragraph，约 220 words。需要验证加上 Limitations 后不超 8 页。如果超页，优先压缩第二段（Relationship to probing methodology）。

The ensemble provides a metric-agnostic selection strategy among principled (threshold-based) metrics. It never significantly underperforms the best individual metric (all $p > 0.27$), and all four models show significant HS advantage over text ($p \leq 0.002$). The ensemble advantage over text ranges from +10.5pp (R1-32B) to +27.0pp (OT-7B). This proof of concept validates that practitioners need not commit to a single metric for layer selection; averaging across metric-selected layers achieves comparable performance. tool_args.new_string:
\paragraph{Implications and novelty.} Our central finding---that metric choice alone produces a 14--61 layer divergence and qualitatively reverses HS advantage conclusions---means safety probing studies should report results under multiple layer selection criteria; layer selection should be treated as a key specification choice alongside model architecture and dataset. The cosine compression mechanism (\cref{app:cosine_volatility}) provides a geometric explanation: shallow-layer representations compress directional information, causing crossing-rate metrics to select layers where probes operate near the noise floor. The cosine compression mechanism is architecture-general (confirmed on Gemma-2; \cref{app:gemma_cross_arch}), though the safety probe application has only been tested on standard attention models. Position partially mediates the advantage (2/4 quadratic); causal interventions on position encoding are needed to disentangle. HarmThoughts is currently the only publicly available dataset with step-level CP annotations; our AdvBench validation confirms the geometric mechanism generalizes beyond this dataset. 1	Reasoning models with chain-of-thought (CoT) can self-jailbreak: their reasoning traces transition from safe deliberation to committed harmful generation without adversarial input. We define the commitment point (CP) as the first reasoning step after which safety deliberation permanently ceases, and compare hidden-state (HS) vs.\ text probes for CP detection across four reasoning LLMs (3 Qwen-family, 1 Llama) on HarmThoughts. The comparison depends critically on which transformer layer is monitored, a sensitivity we show is severe enough to qualitatively reverse safety conclusions: a crossing-rate composite metric selects L0 for R1-8B while threshold-based metrics select L14 (14-layer divergence); at 32B the divergence reaches 61 layers (exploratory$^\dagger$), reversing whether an HS advantage is observed. Threshold-based selection recovers HS precision gains of +20 to +22pp at 7--8B (nested CV) and +15 to +19pp at 32B (exploratory$^\dagger$, $n \leq 20$) over a 384d encoder, but this advantage diminishes with stronger text encoders (4/4 HB at 384d $\to$ 1/4 at 1024d) and partially overlaps with temporal position. Seven alternative methods all fail to match supervised probing. Metric-induced layer selection bias is the robust finding; the HS advantage is conditional on encoder quality and position control.

787	Full per-model temporal ablations are reported in \cref{tab:window_full} (\cref{app:window_ablation}). Key cross-model patterns: (1) R1-8B shows monotonic precision improvement from 69.3\% ($W{=}1$) to 82.2\% ($W{=}25$) with FPR halving (9.65\% to 4.83\%); (2) OT-7B exhibits a split pattern where balanced accuracy peaks at $W{=}3$ while precision and FPR continue improving at larger windows; (3) R1-32B peaks at $W{=}10$ then degrades, likely reflecting overfitting on the small dataset ($n{=}100$); (4) QwQ-32B shows broadly increasing trends with local non-monotonicity. Text probe window ablations (\cref{app:text_window}) show monotonic improvement across all window sizes for both models tested, with larger marginal gains than HS probes (+12.0pp accuracy vs.\ +3.2pp for R1-8B). The asymmetry supports the interpretation that text features benefit proportionally more from temporal context because they encode less information per step.
